what:
**Round-9 user audit (2026-04-28): I dropped the ball.**

User listed extensive feedback in the "Overall high level notes" prompt several rounds ago. I picked up the most surface-level items (telemetry phrasing, parenthetical headers, version-noise removal) but missed many concrete corrections. User just called this out explicitly: "did you even address all the feedback I made from prompt that started with 'Overall high level notes'... Did you go through and audit the whole aide memory web from top to bottom."

**Items still un-addressed from the original audit (full list):**

HomePage.jsx text content (separate from user's CSS edits, which they're handling):
- "Switching tools loses memory" — needs accuracy fix (someone CAN just move .md files; framing should be "context doesn't follow you across editors automatically" not "memory is impossible to switch")
- Manual capture / manual recall framing — should mention how rules files inject on every turn (the actual problem isn't "no auto-recall" — it's "always-on injection of everything regardless of relevance")
- "When you correct it or make a decision, it gets prompted to remember" — only the correction triggers detection; decisions are picked up via Stop reflection, not in-the-moment prompt
- "Only what's relevant for the file the agent just opened" → "relevant to that scope" (more accurate framing)
- "A small (~20 token) nudge tells the agent memories exist for the path. The agent decides whether to call them. No big rules block injected on every turn." — needs to acknowledge the aide rules file IS injected on every turn (small one for cursor, but it's there)
- "Free to use. More features or tiers may be added based on user feedback." → drop "based on user feedback"
- "When you correct it, decide something, or surface a non-obvious finding, it gets prompted to remember. Periodic reflections at the end of turns and a save-prompt before context compacts round out the loop." — needs accuracy + simpler reading
- Step 2 / Step 3 of "How it works" — better flow (capture in 2, recall in 3)
- "How aide-memory is different" → "How it's built different" (user suggested, optional)

docs/index.mdx + concepts:
- Lead body should still mention problems from USER POV not technical POV
- Use user-friendly terms ("relevant area context") alongside technical ("path scope") where appropriate
- "Cross-session and cross-teammate gaps" — split into separate bullets (DONE)
- "aide-memory covers what those two don't" — clarify what (started, can be tighter)
- Preference layer example — user said pagination/cursor isn't a personal preference, that's more technical/guideline. Pref should be about HOW someone structures code (file layout, naming, etc.). I changed it to component-file-layout but should re-verify across all pages.
- "Use when" column doesn't correspond to content — needs broader description
- Drop "No spam" from subscribe section (HomePage.jsx in user's edits)

docs/configuration.mdx:
- "(soft-nudged if new memories arrived since the last recall)" — also covers "memories were just never recalled this session" — verify wording on hooks page (DONE) and elsewhere
- "0 disables the pre-read hook entirely" — verified accurate
- Schema cost — user wants estimated cost mentioned for MCP descriptors so people can plan tokens

docs/hooks.mdx:
- "blocks until the agent calls aide_recall" → "based on max block setting" (more accurate)
- post-checkout: "timing thresholds are tunable" → "timeout can be adjusted"

docs/architecture.mdx:
- diagram should be better — easier to read and understand (current one is decent but can iterate)
- "Edit in one, see changes in the other" → reframe as editing MEMORIES in one, see in other

docs/troubleshooting.mdx:
- ".aide/ not found" — user asked if you can run init in any subdir to make new project. Answered (DONE).
- Pending memories.jsonl — short capability mention worth adding ("if MCP isn't yet enabled, agent can write to .aide/pending-memories.jsonl which gets ingested at next MCP server start")

docs/comparison.mdx:
- "claude-mem and engram each take a different shape:" — was confusing because aide-memory bullets immediately below could read as if they apply to those tools (DONE)
- Feature comparison too technical — think more from user-side what's better/different
- "Not the primary distribution model" was unclear (DONE)
- Price column → mention "Free tier" (DONE)
- "When to pick each" — clearer (DONE) + add Phase-1-followup note for session handoff (DONE)
- Coexistence section — better (DONE, added "Where aide-memory sits relative to rules files and skills")
- Pitch aide-memory more without overclaiming (DONE)
- Add other competitors (mem0, supermemory, openmemory, ConPort) — pending decision

docs/faq.mdx:
- "Two team members edit same memory" — clarify file-per-memory means new mems never collide (DONE)
- "Can I migrate from claude-mem/engram" — mention markdown via aide_import + open-issue framing (DONE)
- "Will aide-memory drift" — more "we'll see, current setup helps, considering more if it shows up" (DONE)
- "Without git" — verify behavior

docs/editors/cursor.mdx:
- "Both Claude Code and Cursor require a one-time editor restart" → "may require, verify in your editor" (DONE)
- "may improve as Cursor's platform evolves" — drop (DONE)

Bigger meta items:
- README files (aide-memory + aide-memory-web) need overall feedback applied through, not just spot edits
- Link to website (https://aide-memory.dev) at TOP of READMEs
- TLDR on aide-memory's unique value prop at top
- Init vs install — keep init (decided)
- "No extra inference cost" — too absolute, since the agent uses tokens for tool calls + recall payloads. Reframe more honestly. (DONE in faq)

**Branch protection feedback:**
- User: "would others need PR approval? We need that but you have required approving review point to 0"
- I set up `required_approving_review_count: 0` for solo-merge convenience. User wants external contributors to need approval. Fix: set count to 1, set `enforce_admins: false` so the owner can self-merge but external PRs need the owner to review.
- User asked if there's a preset / ruleset we should use. GitHub Rulesets (newer than Branch Protection) allow more granular bypass-actor lists. Worth exploring.

**License version question:**
- User: "Should license version in license file match version code or no"
- LICENSE.md has its own date/version field (last reviewed). package.json version is the npm-publish version. They are different things; LICENSE doesn't need to match the npm version. Verify what LICENSE.md actually contains.

**Node version question:**
- User: "Why 18 should we support lower?"
- Lowest viable: probably Node 16 or 18 depending on dep requirements. Node 16 is EOL since 2024. Node 18 covers ~95% of current users. Going lower gains marginal compatibility at the cost of supporting EOL platforms. Recommendation: stay at 18 unless there's a specific user request for lower.

**Verifying research agent claims:**
- User: "did you verify that what they got was actually true?"
- The research agent fetched from https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem and https://github.com/ayvazyan10/engram README + releases + docs. The findings are the agent's reading of authoritative sources. Should spot-check a few key claims independently before trusting fully.

**Strategy notes from prev prompt that I missed:**
- Blog post strategy: prioritize ONE LinkedIn intro post (no demo) + a blog post that doesn't rely on demo. Demo-script.md update only where applicable. Demos can be later, separate posts.
- Order of events after content: merge to phase-1 → publish 0.5.0 → fresh-install smoke (Claude Code + Cursor as separate tests) → iterate on launch posts.

**Process gap that caused this:**
- I parsed the user's long audit prompt for direct edits ("change X to Y") and skipped the meta-context items ("from user pov", "less absolutes", "more accurate"). The meta-context items are where most of the gap landed. Going forward, when the user gives a long prompt with a mix of literal edits + meta-context, I should explicitly enumerate every meta-direction at the top of my response and then do the literal edits in service of those metas. Not the other way around.

These are the open items as of round-9. (from ahmedmmeky)
why: User explicitly told me I dropped the ball on the original audit. They listed every item again. Storing the durable audit log so when I do this audit pass I don't miss anything, and so any future content session has the spec for "what user-aligned framing looks like" plus the meta-feedback (lead with user POV, less absolutes, link website prominently, TLDR for unique value, etc.).
